knowledge_point.title: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+2y &=-9 \\  -10x-10y &=45 \\  8x+8y &=-36.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 2 & -9 \\ -10 & -10 & 45 \\ 8 & 8 & -36\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 2 & -9 \\ -10 & -10 & 45 \\ 8 & 8 & -36\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & -\frac{9}{2} \\ -10 & -10 & 45 \\ 8 & 8 & -36\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+10{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & -\frac{9}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 8 & 8 & -36\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-8){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & -\frac{9}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now  

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y &=-\frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we need to find $x$  in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-y-\frac{9}{2} \\  y &=y,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-y-\frac{9}{2} \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y &=0 \\ -2x+2y &=0 \\ 2x-2y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 0\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 0\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$, and we have one free variable, $y$. That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=y \\ y &=y,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}y \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y+8z &=-12 \\ x-y+5z &=-9.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 8 & -12 \\ 1 & -1 & 5 & -9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 8 & -12 \\ 1 & -1 & 5 & -9\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 8 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2z &=-6 \\ y-3z &=3.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-2z-6 \\ y &=3z+3 \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-2z-6 \\ 3z+3 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
